target_customer: Mid and large employers in Latin America in retail, manufacturing and hospitality, plus service workers seeking jobs
problem: Employers in Mexico struggle with hiring and retaining hourly service staff and managing shifts, attendance and performance.
business_model: B2B SaaS HR modules plus a hiring marketplace for service workers
product_category: HR software and hospitality jobs marketplace

founders.name: Ignacio Martinez
founders.background_notes: Named CEO in Contxto (2019-05-09). Contxto says the founders drew on their own restaurant backgrounds.

investors: Google for Startups Accelerator: Latin Founders

technical_complexity.rationale: Shift planning, geolocated check-in with facial recognition and a multi-module HR suite. Standard SaaS engineering with some hard parts in facial recognition.

defensibility.rationale: HR data and processes create some switching costs once embedded, but modules were individually common.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found on incumbent response.

market_need_then: Contxto (2019-05) said the founders aimed to improve hiring and retention for service workers. No spend data found.

branding.domain_note: Product used alana.jobs. That domain is now parked and listed for sale.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand. The name is a first name and the product also appeared as Alana Jobs, which blurred it between HR software and a jobs marketplace.

outcome_analysis: Alana started as a hospitality jobs marketplace in Mexico, got an undisclosed investment from DILA Capital in May 2019, and joined YC with a broader HR suite and 14 staff. A database lists later grant-style funding in 2020. No shutdown report was found and the domain is now parked, so the cause of becoming inactive is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: DILA investment reported by Contxto and LAVCA, amount undisclosed. The 2020-11 Google for Startups round rests on a single database (CB Insights), which reports 150K total raised over 5 rounds, so other rounds may be missing. Dated competitor sources near the batch were not found, so the list is empty. Worky is a later or undated Mexican HR competitor, not recorded.
